results.title: Get started with Front's MCP server [beta]
excerpts:
Get started with Front's MCP server

Edited
⚠️ Front’s MCP server allows external AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT) to connect to Front.
* If you’re looking to connect in the opposite direction and allow Front’s AI to connect an external tool, follow the steps for MCP Connectors .
* To let an AI tool manage your Front settings instead (rules, inboxes, AI agents), see Get started with Front's Admin MCP server .

Overview

Front's MCP server lets you and your teammates connect Front to AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot. Once connected, the AI assistant can use your conversations, draft replies, leave internal comments, and take other actions on your behalf — all while respecting the user permissions set within Front.
Because Front handles every channel — email, SMS, chat, and more — in one place, the AI assistant gets the full context of a conversation: messages across all channels, internal comments, tag and assignment history, and rule actions, all in one timeline.
Head to Front Community to read the official announcement and get the starter guide with ready-to-use templates for the MCP.

What is the MCP server?

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI assistants connect to external tools. The MCP server specifically enables external AI assistants and similar tools to access a predetermined set of Front data and actions. Connecting to the Front MCP server means the AI assistant can do things like search your inbox, read a thread, draft a reply, leave an internal comment, or tag a conversation — as you, with your permissions.
Think of it as giving the AI assistant a key to Front that only works while you're authorized, and only does the things your role already allows.

What you can do with it

Here are some common ways to put the MCP server to work:
Triage your inbox
"Look at my Open inbox and help me prioritize what to respond to first. Flag anything that mentions billing or churn risk."
Draft higher quality replies with broader context
"Find the most recent conversation with [customer].

...

There are two ways to connect, depending on what your workspace and your AI client support.

Option 1: Official connector in your AI assistant's directory

The simplest path is finding Front in the connector directory of your AI assistant of choice and connecting in a few clicks.
If your AI assistant is managed by your company — as it often is in larger organizations — your IT or business systems team will need to allow the Front connector before it appears in your account. If you don't see it listed, that's the team to ask.
Available now:
* Claude — is available in the Claude connector directory .
* ChatGPT or Codex — is available in the OpenAI plugin directory .
To connect via an official directory:
* A Front admin (or any user authorized to install integrations from the Front App Store) must connect via the directory links above.
* Then, any user in your company can use the directory links to connect their own accounts.
We're prioritizing directory listings based on customer demand. If your team relies on an AI assistant we haven't listed, let us know in the Front Community — that's how we decide what to add next.
If your AI assistant's directory doesn't have Front yet, you can still connect today using the custom path below.

Option 2: Custom connection (available now in any MCP-compatible client)

If you want to use Front in an MCP client that doesn't (yet) have an official directory listing — or if you're building your own internal agent — your workspace admin can create a private developer app in Front and use its credentials to connect.
Setup involves creating the app in Front, configuring OAuth scopes, and pointing your MCP client at mcp.frontapp.com/mcp . Full instructions live in the Front Developer Portal .

How are permissions controlled?

For both connection options, Front admins can limit which read/write/send permissions the MCP server can use. These selected permissions define the full set (superset) of data and actions the MCP server can access. From there, each connected teammate is still restricted to what their own Front permissions allow. For example, your company might enable MCP server access for all Front inboxes, but because each teammate must sign in to their own Front account, the MCP server for that teammate will only be able to access the inboxes they can access in Front.

...

* Option 2: Custom connector — the permissions are controlled by the Front admin who creates the developer app in Front, as described in our Developer Portal . When configuring the app in Front, the admin restricts the read/write/send permissions the MCP server can use, and that becomes the superset for any AI assistant connecting through it.
In both cases, the MCP server for that user is still restricted to what their Front role allows.

What's supported today

The MCP server currently lets you:
* Search and read conversations across every channel (email, SMS, chat, custom)
* Draft and send replies on the conversation's native channel
* Read and post internal comments
* Tag, assign, and change conversation status
* Search and update contacts
* See teammates, inboxes, and teams
More capabilities are in the works. To see the latest capabilities, simply ask your AI assistant what tools are available once you're connected.

Join the community

Check out how others are using the MCP server. The MCP space in the Front Community is the place to:
* See what others are building and share your own workflows
* Ask questions and get help connecting
* Submit feedback and feature requests

results.title: Get started with Front's Admin MCP server [open beta]
excerpts:
Get started with Front's Admin MCP server [open beta]

Edited
⚠️ Important to know:
* This feature is in beta. This article may require final changes before the feature is released to general availability (GA).
* Front's Admin MCP server allows external AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT) to manage your Front settings. To let an AI tool work with your conversations instead, see Get started with Front's MCP server . To let Front's AI connect to an external tool, follow the steps for MCP Connectors .

Overview

Front's Admin MCP server lets Front admins connect AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT to their Front settings. Once connected, the AI assistant can read how your Front instance is set up and create or edit rules, inboxes, tags, message templates, knowledge bases, AI agents, and more, from a request written in plain language.
Every change is made as the admin who connected, only within what their Front role allows, and shows in your audit log .
Use it for configuration work that is slow to do by hand: auditing hundreds of rules, applying the same change across many of them, or setting up and testing an AI agent.

What is the Admin MCP server?

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI assistants connect to external tools. The Admin MCP server gives an AI assistant a set of tools to read and change your Front configuration, the same work you would otherwise do in your settings one item at a time.
It is separate from Front's MCP server. The MCP server works with conversations on behalf of any teammate. The Admin MCP server works with your settings on behalf of an admin.
Think of it as giving your AI assistant access to your Front settings, with your admin role as the limit: it can only change what you could change yourself.

...

Connecting Front to your AI assistant

There are two ways to connect, depending on what your AI assistant supports.

Option 1: Official connector in your AI assistant's directory

The simplest path is to find Admin MCP in the connector directory of your AI assistant and connect in a few clicks.
If your AI assistant is managed by your company, as it often is in larger organizations, your IT or business systems team may need to allow the connector before it appears in your account. If you don't see it listed, that's the team to ask.
* Claude — is available in the Claude connector directory .
To connect via an official directory:
* A Front company admin connects first, using the directory links above.
* Then any company or workspace admin at your company can use the same links to connect their own account.

Custom connection (any MCP-compatible client)

If you're building your own internal agent, a company admin can create a private developer app in Front and use its credentials to connect.
Setup involves creating a developer app with the Front Admin MCP feature, choosing its permissions, and pointing your MCP client at mcp.frontapp.com/admin-mcp . You need a separate developer app from the one you use for Front's MCP server. Full instructions are in the Front Developer Portal .

Who can connect?

Company admins and workspace admins. Teammates without admin permissions and AI agents can't connect.
* Company admins can work across your whole company.
* Workspace admins can only change the workspaces they administer, and don't see tools for company-level resources such as AI agents, knowledge bases, and custom fields.

How are permissions controlled?

For both connection options, admins can limit the read and write permissions the Admin MCP server can use, resource by resource (for example, read-only access to AI agents). These permissions define the full set (superset) of what any connected admin can do through it. From there, each admin is still limited to what their own Front role allows.

...

* Create and edit inboxes, tags, message templates, views, custom fields, task templates, shifts, and teammate groups, and invite teammates
* Set up AI agents: instructions, tone, Playbooks, knowledge sources, and connectors
* Create, edit, and publish knowledge base articles
* Test AI agents with simulations and simulation criteria, and review Opportunities and AI replies

...

FAQ

What's the difference between Front's MCP server and the Admin MCP server?

Front's MCP server lets any teammate's AI assistant work with conversations: search, read, reply, comment, tag, and assign. The Admin MCP server lets an admin's AI assistant work with Front settings: rules, inboxes, AI agents, and more. They're separate connections, and you can use both at the same time.

Will the tools change during the beta?

...

Why don't I see some tools?

Tools depend on your role and plan. Workspace admins don't see tools for company-level resources. Some tools only appear when your plan includes the matching feature: for example, simulation tools need Autopilot, shift tools need Shifts, and connector tools need custom application connectors.

Should I use Admin Copilot or the Admin MCP server?

results.title: Understanding Connectors - Front Help Center
excerpts:
Understanding Connectors

Edited
⚠️ MCP Connectors allow Front’s AI to connect to an external tool. If you’re looking to connect in the opposite direction and allow external AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT) to connect to Front, follow the steps for Front’s MCP server .

Overview

Connectors let Front integrate with the outside tools your team already uses, so you can bring their data and actions right inside Front. A Connector is one connection to a third-party system: once it's set up, Front can read information from that system and make changes in it.
There are three types of Connectors, based on how Front connects to the tool:
* Application requests: Call a tool's API to fetch data or take an action, like looking up an order or updating a record.
* Application objects: Pull a specific record from a tool (an order, a shipment, a ticket) into the conversation and keep it in sync.
* MCP Connectors: Connect to a tool's own set of actions (its MCP server) so Front's AI can use them directly.
You use Connectors in two places:
* In your workflows — rules, macros, and chatbots run a Connector at set points, in a set order.
* With Front's AI — Copilot, Autopilot, and AI steps in your workflows can use a Connector on their own, deciding when to call it as they work.
Application requests and application objects work in both your workflows and with Front’s AI. MCP connections are used by Front's AI.

Types of Connectors

Application objects

Application objects are a simple way to get information from a third-party system and display it as a comment or link inside a Front conversation.
For example, if a customer is writing in to your support team to ask about a specific order, Front can detect the order ID in conversation messages or comments and automatically attach a link to the order object in your external system.

...

MCP Connectors

An MCP Connector links Front to a tool's own set of actions, so Front's AI can use them directly, with no custom building. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that tools use to publish what they're able to do. When a tool supports it, Front connects to that published set of actions, rather than you configuring each API call yourself.
What sets MCP Connectors apart from application requests and objects is who decides when to act. With a rule or macro, you specify the trigger and the order of operations ahead of time. With an MCP Connector, Front's AI decides in the moment whether an action is needed, which one fits, and what to do with the result.

...

Custom Connectors

Build your own application request or application object , or connect your own MCP server in Developer settings.

Managing Connectors

Connectors settings

Company admins manage Connectors in Connectors section in company settings. This is where you can:
* Browse available Connectors and see a short description of what each one does before connecting.
* Connect a new tool, and see its status once connected.
* Choose which of a Connector's actions are turned on, and which features can use it.
* Check connection health, reconnect if access expires, or disconnect a tool you no longer use.
Custom-built Connectors configured in Developer settings are managed there for now; they'll move into the Connectors section in a future update.

Overview of Front's API and use cases

Edited

Overview

Front’s platform features a variety of APIs that allow you to build custom workflows and user interfaces that can dramatically improve the quality and efficiency of your customer communication. Our APIs are simple to use and include detailed documentation with walkthroughs, code examples, and more. Most custom integrations can be built in only 1-3 weeks.
If you’re interested in learning more about our platform or are looking for guidance on a particular workflow you’d like to build, feel free to reach out to your account manager or post in our Front Community . We’re here to help you strategize what workflows would be most helpful for your team, and to dive into the technical implementation details.
For some great examples of what some other customers have built with Front’s platform, feel free to check out our Flow and Tell contest winners. We also have dozens of partner integrations that can be installed with just a few clicks.
Front’s platform is made up of three primary APIs: Core API, Plugin SDK, and Channel API

Core API

The Core API is Front’s “backend” API that allows developers to access and update almost all elements in Front, including messages, contacts, channels, inboxes, teammates, analytics and more. The API also includes webhooks support to enable real-time updates from Front to your system.

Developer resources for building API integrations

Edited

Overview

Front provides developers the following resources for building integrations with our APIs and SDKs.

Developer Community

The Developer Community is a space to ask technical questions, submit API feedback, and engage with your fellow developers and with our Platform team. Visit community.front.com to join the conversation!

Developer Portal

The Developer Portal contains documentation for the Front Platform APIs and SDKs, as well as sample code and useful tools for development. Visit dev.frontapp.com to get started.
Follow the instructions on the Developer Portal to create a free developer account to begin building integrations on the Front Platform.

Developer Settings in Front

The Developers page in Front's company settings allows you to manage the configuration and features of the apps you build on the Front Platform. Through the Developers page, you can create new apps, edit existing apps, manage integration listing assets, and choose whether to publish an app to all Front customers or keep it private to one instance.
To learn about the Developers page, refer to the Create, manage, and publish apps topic on the Developer Portal.

# Get started with Front's MCP server

Edited

⚠️ **Front’s MCP server allows external AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT) to connect to Front.** If you’re looking to connect in the opposite direction and allow Front’s AI to connect an external tool, follow the steps for MCP Connectors.

## Overview

Front's MCP server lets you and your teammates connect Front to AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot. Once connected, the AI assistant can use your conversations, draft replies, leave internal comments, and take other actions on your behalf — all while respecting the user permissions set within Front.

Because Front handles every channel — email, SMS, chat, and more — in one place, the AI assistant gets the full context of a conversation: messages across all channels, internal comments, tag and assignment history, and rule actions, all in one timeline.

Head to Front Community to read the official announcement and get the starter guide with ready-to-use templates for the MCP.

---

## What is the MCP server?

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI assistants connect to external tools. The *MCP server* specifically enables external AI assistants and similar tools to access a predetermined set of Front data and actions. Connecting to the Front MCP server means the AI assistant can do things like search your inbox, read a thread, draft a reply, leave an internal comment, or tag a conversation — as you, with your permissions.

**Think of it as giving the AI assistant a key to Front that only works while you're authorized, and only does the things your role already allows.**

---

## What you can do with it

Here are some common ways to put the MCP server to work:

**Triage your inbox**

> "Look at my Open inbox and help me prioritize what to respond to first. Flag anything that mentions billing or churn risk."

**Draft higher quality replies with broader context**

> "Find the most recent conversation with [customer]. Cross-reference their account in Salesforce, then draft a reply that addresses their question and acknowledges where they are in the renewal cycle."

**Investigate a bug rep
...

**Available now:**

* **Claude** — is available in the Claude connector directory.
* **ChatGPT or Codex** — is available in the OpenAI plugin directory.

To connect via an official directory:

* A Front admin (or any user authorized to install integrations from the Front App Store) must connect via the directory links above.
* Then, any user in your company can use the directory links to connect their own accounts.

We're prioritizing directory listings based on customer demand. If your team relies on an AI assistant we haven't listed, let us know in the Front Community — that's how we decide what to add next.

If your AI assistant's directory doesn't have Front yet, you can still connect today using the custom path below.

### Option 2: Custom connection (available now in any MCP-compatible client)

If you want to use Front in an MCP client that doesn't (yet) have an official directory listing — or if you're building your own internal agent — your workspace admin can create a private developer app in Front and use its credentials to connect.

Setup involves creating the app in Front, configuring OAuth scopes, and pointing your MCP client at `mcp.frontapp.com/mcp`. Full instructions live in the Front Developer Portal.

---

## How are permissions controlled?

For both connection options, Front admins can limit which read/write/send permissions the MCP server can use. These selected permissions define the full set (superset) of data and actions the MCP server can access.
